transcription.tex: 1. A particle has velocity \(v=\tfrac12t^3\) m/s. Find its velocity after 4 s, and the time when \(v=108\) m/s.\par 2. Another particle has \(v=2t^2-16t+24\), for \(t\ge0\). Find:\par a. initial velocity;\par b. times at rest;\par c. time when \(v=64\);\par d. greatest speed on \(0\le t\le5\).
d. Check endpoints and \(v\)’s turning point:\[v(0)=24,\]\[v(4)=-8,\]\[v(5)=-6.\]\par Greatest speed \(=24\) m/s.

transcription.tex: A particle \(P\) moves on the \(x\)-axis. At time \(t\) seconds the velocity of \(P\) is \(v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in the direction of \(x\) increasing, where \(v=8t-2t^2\). When \(t=0\), \(P\) is at the origin \(O\). Find: \par (a) the time taken for the particle to come to instantaneous rest \par (b) the greatest speed of the particle in the interval \(0\le t\le4\).
(a) a. \(2t(4-t)=0\). The next time is \(t=4\) s.
(b) b. Velocity is non-negative throughout the interval.\[\frac{dv}{dt}=8-4t=0\Rightarrow t=2.\]\par \(v(2)=8\) m/s; both endpoint velocities are zero. Greatest speed: 8 m/s.

transcription.tex: At time t = 0, a particle moves in a straight horizontal line from a point O, then returns to the starting point. The distance, s metres, from the point O at time t seconds is given by: \(s=3t^2-t^3,\ 0\le t\le T\). Given that the model is valid when \(s\ge0\), find the value of \(T\). Explain your answer.
\[s=t^2(3-t).\]\par The non-zero root is \(t=3\). For \(t>3\), the expression becomes negative and cannot represent distance.
The particle returns to \(O\) at \(T=3\) s. The stated distance model ends there.

transcription.tex: A particle \(P\) moves in a straight line. At time \(t\) seconds the acceleration of \(P\) is \(a\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) and the velocity \(v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) is given by \(v=kt-3t^2\), where \(k\) is a constant. The initial acceleration of \(P\) is \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). \par (a) Find the value of \(k\). \par (b) Using the value of \(k\) found in part (a), find the acceleration when \(P\) is instantaneously at rest.
(b) At rest \(v=t(4-3t)=0\), so \(t=0\) or \(t=4/3\) s. The initial acceleration is \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). At the subsequent instant of rest, \(a=4-6(4/3)=-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

transcription.tex: A yo-yo’s distance below the hand is\[s=0.6t+0.4t^2-0.2t^3,\quad0\le t\le3.\]\par a. Justify the time restriction.\par b. Find the maximum distance from the hand to 3 s.f.
a. \(s=\tfrac15t(3-t)(1+t)\). It is non-negative for \(0\le t\le3\), returning to the hand at \(t=3\).
b. \(v=0.6+0.8t-0.6t^2=0\).\[t=\frac{2+\sqrt{13}}3=1.8685\ldots\]\par The other root is negative. Substitution gives maximum distance 1.21 m.

transcription.tex: A particle \(P\) starts at the origin \(O\) at time \(t=0\) and moves along the \(x\)-axis. At time \(t\) seconds the distance of the particle, \(s\) m, from the origin is given by \(s=\frac{9t^2}2-t^3,\ 0\le t\le4.5\). \par (a) Sketch a displacement–time graph for the motion of \(P\). \par (b) Hence justify the restriction \(0\le t\le4.5\). \par (c) Find the maximum distance of the particle from \(O\). \par (d) Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle at this point.
a–b a–b. \(s=t^2(4.5-t)\): starts with a horizontal tangent at \((0,0)\), rises to a maximum, then returns to \((4.5,0)\). Beyond 4.5 s it is negative, so cannot represent distance.
(c) c. \(v=9t-3t^2=3t(3-t)\).\par The maximum occurs at \(t=3\): \(s=13.5\) m.

transcription.tex: A train moves in a straight line along a 4 km test track. The motion of the train is modelled as a particle travelling in a straight line, and the distance, s m, of the train from the start of the track after time t seconds is given by \(s=3.6t+1.76t^2-0.02t^3,\ 0\le t\le90\). Show that the train never reaches the end of the track.

Velocity changes from positive to negative at \(59.672\) s, giving the maximum.\[s_{\max}=2230\text{ m (3 s.f.)}<4000\text{ m}.\]\par The train never reaches the end. Negative later displacement means it has passed the starting point in the opposite direction.

transcription.tex: A particle has velocity \(v=5-3t^2\) m/s, \(t\ge0\). Find the distance travelled in the third second of its motion.
The third second is \(2\le t\le3\). Velocity is negative throughout this interval, so distance is the negative of displacement.

transcription.tex: A particle P moves on the positive x-axis. The velocity of P at time t seconds is (2t² − 9t + 4) \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). When t = 0, P is 15 m from the origin O. Find \par (a) the values of t when P is instantaneously at rest, (3) \par (b) the acceleration of P when t = 5, (3) \par (c) the total distance travelled by P in the interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 5. (5)

c. Integrate: \(x=\tfrac23t^3-\tfrac92t^2+4t+15\).\par Velocity changes sign at both rest times. Add the three positive distances:\[\tfrac{23}{24}+\tfrac{343}{24}+\tfrac{25}{6}=\tfrac{233}{12}\text{ m}.\]
